blocks.html: Fixed income tells a similar story; the Federal Reserve delivered its third rate cut of 2025 and signaled that short- term rates were approachingneutral. Since the 10-year Treasury yield was comparativelystable, the 2s/10s curve moved from ~ 56 basis points at the start of the quarter to ~ 71 basis points by the end of the quarter. These moves were accompanied by a meaningful shift in policy expectations for 2026; forecasts of roughly two 25- basis-point cuts in 2026 at the beginning of the quarter revised to expectations of zero to one cut. Additionally, a ~ 5.8% increase in the Bloomberg Commodity Index (driven primarily by broad strength in metals) suggests that inflation may surprise the market to the upside in 2026.

blocks.html: Importantly, Basepoint’s borrowers continue to see unchanged credit performance. We believe this is due to the continued employment availability for blue-collar workers. There are increasing anecdotes about the dichotomy between the outlook for white-collar and blue-collar workers. As Jensen Huang (NVIDIA CEO) recently said, “The skilled craft segment of every economy is going to see a boom… You’re going to have to be doubling and doubling and doubling every single year.” Similarly, Jim Farley (Ford CEO) recently said, “Hiring an entry worker at a tech company has fallen 50% since 2019 … Artificial intelligence is gonna replace literally half of all white-collar workers in the U.S.”Basepoint’s borrowers primarily support blue-collar workers: mechanics, plumbers, nurses and other professionals whose skills remain in high demand. According to the Deep Future Analytics’ shared pool data for consumer loans, bureau score adjustments indicate that performance for the Subprime universe, the sector of the market BasePoint’s borrowers have exposure to, is materially better overall than the Near-prime, Prime and even Super-prime segments.

blocks.html: Although it was not a fourth quarter event, it is important to comment briefly on President Trump’s proposal to impose a temporary 10% interest rate cap for credit cards. While 2026 is an election year and politics can be unpredictable, we view the odds of restricting all forms of credit to be low, even if enacted for banks. As Jamie Dimon (JPMorgan CEO) recently said, “You'd have to have a drastic reduction of the credit card business …it would remove credit from 80% of Americans.“Regardless of one’s political views, many consumers simply do not qualify for unsecured rates anywhere near 10% and would likely lose access to credit under such a plan.Having said that, if only banks were impacted, BasePoint’s borrowers would likely be large beneficiaries.

First payment default rates have remained stable ranging from 6-8% over the past twelve months.

blocks.html: NCP Holdings, L.P. (“NCP”), founded in 2005 by Lee Schear, is the holding company of NCP Finance and affiliated entities. NCP Finance or its affiliates originate a variety of consumer loans including installment, title and short-term cash advances brokered by their Credit Service Organizations (“CSO”) partners in the state of Texas under NCP’s CSO Program. blocks.text: BP PMKN LLC (“BP PMKN”), a wholly-owned subsidiary of BasePoint Capital III LLC, has agreed to acquire International Personal Finance plc (“IPF”), a British financial services provider operating in nine markets across Eastern Europe, Mexico and Australia. BP PMKN Eurobond represents cash collateral deposited into escrow in advance of the acquisition.

blocks.html: In December 2025, BP PMKN LLC (“BP PMKN”), a wholly-owned subsidiary of BasePoint Capital III LLC, provided interim bridge financing (the “Bridge Financing”) to its wholly owned acquisition vehicle, IPF Parent Holdings Limited (“UK Bidco”) for the pending acquisition of IPF. Under the UK Takeover Code, a bidder must demonstrate that it has suﬃcient financial resources to implement the oﬀer by the time a firm intention to make an oﬀer is announced. This UK process of a deal’s “cash confirmation” is typically satisfied through committed financing arrangements from banks or other institutions or by having funds readily available (for example, cash on hand or placed in escrow). To satisfy these requirements, BP PMKN funded an escrow account on behalf of UK Bidco in the amount of $549,602,200 to satisfy “cash confirmation” requirements. The funding was documented through two instruments (i) a $274,801,100 USD- denominated note issued by UK Bidco (the “Eurobond”) and (ii) a $274,801,100 secured promissory note issued by BP PMKN. BasePoint expects to refinance the Bridge Financing in full at or shortly prior to the closing of the acquisition. The Fund will have the option, but will not be obligated, to participate in the permanent financing of the acquisition. If the acquisition does not close, the funds in the escrow account will be released from the escrow account and returned to BP PMKN.
